name: IN-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Messmer renominated and out-raising Allen about 4-to-1
No polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The R+18 district, Messmer's incumbency and clear fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Republican win near 96% all point the same way, with no evidence of a Democratic opening. The forecast stays at a Safe R rating with a roughly 17-point Republican margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Messmer under 55% or a surge of Democratic outside spending would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Indiana's 8th District is deeply Republican territory, and first-term incumbent Mark Messmer enters the general election after clearing his primary. He has raised about $1.2 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Mary Allen, who has brought in under $300,000. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Messmer roughly a 96% chance of winning.

The fundamentals align with that picture: the district's partisan lean, the incumbency advantage, and the money gap all favor the Republican side. Barring an unexpected shift, Messmer is positioned for a comfortable win in November.
